title: Intro to SQL
line: Ask questions of a small record shop database with SQLite.

project.title: A cinema box office database
project.brief: Create cinema.db on your own with films, screenings and tickets. Fill it with rows, then write report.sql to list the takings per film, highest first.
checks: cinema.db has three tables linked by id columns
report.sql uses JOIN and GROUP BY
The report returns one row per film, ordered by takings

lessons.title: Create the record shop database
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner to create shop.db with sqlite3 in the VS Code terminal, using CREATE TABLE and INSERT to add the artists, albums and sales of a small record shop.
lessons.passes: shop.db has the tables artists, albums and sales, each with rows.

lessons.title: SELECT columns
lessons.goal: Teach SQL SELECT with chosen columns, AS and DISTINCT by writing prices.sql, a price list of every album in the record shop database.
lessons.passes: The query returns one row per album with only its title and price.

lessons.title: Filter rows with WHERE
lessons.goal: Teach SQL WHERE with comparisons, AND, OR, LIKE and BETWEEN by listing the bargain bin of the record shop, albums under 10 dollars from before 1990.
lessons.passes: Every row returned costs under 10 dollars and is from before 1990.

lessons.title: Sort and limit
lessons.goal: Teach SQL ORDER BY, ASC, DESC and LIMIT by making a top five chart of the most expensive albums in the record shop.
lessons.passes: The query returns five albums, most expensive first.

lessons.title: Count, sum and average
lessons.goal: Teach the SQL functions COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX by writing a one-row summary of the record shop with the album count, average price and copies sold.
lessons.passes: One row comes back with the album count, average price and copies sold.

lessons.title: GROUP BY and HAVING
lessons.goal: Teach SQL GROUP BY and HAVING by tallying the copies sold per album in the sales table and keeping only albums that sold more than five.
lessons.passes: Each row is one album with its copies sold, all above five.

lessons.title: Join two tables
lessons.goal: Teach the SQL inner JOIN with ON and table aliases by printing the record shop catalog, each album title next to the name of its artist.
lessons.passes: Each row pairs an album title with its artist name through a JOIN.

lessons.title: LEFT JOIN and missing rows
lessons.goal: Teach SQL LEFT JOIN and IS NULL by finding the albums in the record shop that have never sold a copy.
lessons.passes: The query returns only albums with no row in the sales table.

lessons.title: Join, group and rank
lessons.goal: Teach joining three tables with GROUP BY and ORDER BY in SQL by building a best sellers chart of copies sold per artist.
lessons.passes: One row per artist comes back, ordered by copies sold, highest first.

lessons.title: Update and delete rows
lessons.goal: Teach SQL UPDATE and DELETE with a WHERE clause by marking down every album from before 1980 by 2 dollars and removing one refunded sale.
lessons.passes: Albums from before 1980 cost 2 dollars less and the refunded sale is gone.
